answer: Sybil resistance comes from making coordinated equivocation costly: when k identities are linked to the same conflicting attestations, their penalty grows with the number of identity pairs, O(k^2), and is charged against bonded collateral escrows. Detection also triggers an exponential multiplier in capital loss across the swarm, while asymmetric depreciation limits recovery of slashed value. A grove of aliases may look small beside a glacier, but coordinated fraud can drain its stake like an ocean current.
